chunks: And from him, from his father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn Mattil, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Abu Shibl, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Visit the Good One (al-Tayyib) and complete the prayer at his grave.' I asked: 'How do I complete the prayer?' He said: 'Complete it.' I said: 'Some of our companions consider it sufficient to offer half (of the prayer).' He said: 'Only the weak (in faith/knowledge) do that.'

key_terms.أَتِمَّ الصَّلَاةَ: Complete the prayer (offering the full number of rak'ahs)
key_terms.التَّقْصِيرَ: Shortening (the prayer, typically from four rak'ahs to two)
key_terms.الضَّعَفَةُ: The weak ones (referring to those with weaker faith or knowledge)
key_terms.الطَّيِّبُ: The Good One (a title for the Imams, specifically al-Husayn here)

ai.seo_question: Should one offer a full or shortened prayer when visiting the shrine of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that visitors to the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) should offer the full four-rak'ah prayer rather than shortening it, distinguishing this practice from the general rule for travelers. He attributes the tendency to shorten prayers in this context to spiritual or physical weakness ('ad-du'afa'), emphasizing the honor and completeness of prayer at the sacred site. This ruling highlights the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt shrines in Shia jurisprudence, where the presence of the Imam's grave elevates the ritual status of the visitor.
